I will do it close to what I did before, because 15 mu is not small for two people, and I cannot gamble with the harvest. I have farmed many years, so I start from what worked in my own field and what I saw nearby. For the wheat-maize land, I will keep most of the ground in that rotation because with well water it is steady money. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more watching and more spraying, but if I manage it well it still brings cash. I will not cut fertilizer too hard. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss hurts more than wasting one bag. So for wheat I will feed it enough at sowing and again later, with 3 waterings if the weather asks for it. For maize I will sow fast after wheat, keep the stand even, give it strong nitrogen, and water it twice. For cotton I will not spread too much land, but on the cotton I keep I will use more potassium and spray more times, because if insects get ahead of me, the field goes bad quickly. I will use the same way of working as last year, only keeping the better seed where I can afford it and not trying fancy new things.
